summary: This version of the RobotPet class guards its battery level: instead of storing whatever number it is handed, it clamps the value into the range 0 to 100. The charge() method adds to the battery and relies on that guard to stop at a full charge.

lines.text: Even inside the constructor, this assignment goes through the battery setter rather than storing the value directly, so a robot pet created with a battery of 150 starts at 100.
The @property decorator turns battery into an attribute that is really a method call, so pet.battery still reads like plain data while the class keeps control of it.
The setter is the gatekeeper: every time anything writes to pet.battery, this method runs first and decides what actually gets stored.
The underscore name is where the real value lives. Writing self._battery here rather than self.battery is essential, because assigning to self.battery would call the setter again and loop forever.
Because charge() adds through the property instead of touching _battery, the clamping happens automatically, and this is exactly the behaviour the unit test for charge() will check.
